page: Vultr vcg-a16-3c-32g-8vram is a Cloud GPU server configured with an x86_64 architecture. It features 3 dedicated physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.0 GHz, with 3 vCPUs and a single thread per core. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 10.67 GB of RAM per core. For acceleration, it includes a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A16 GPU with 8 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is provided by a 170 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate moderate single-core capabilities alongside weaker multi-core and memory performance. The Intel Xeon processor achieved a single-core Geekbench score of 1291.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1684.62. However, multi-core performance is limited, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 3212.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 5491.32, both falling into the lower performance tiers. Memory bandwidth is also relatively low, measuring 29.39 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 22.45 GB/sec for large-block write operations.

The fractional NVIDIA Ampere A16 GPU with 8 GB VRAM is suited for lightweight parallel processing tasks. In LLM inference benchmarks using a small 135M parameter model, the server achieved average performance with 494.21 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 121.1 tokens/sec for text generation. However, performance drops significantly on larger models, with prompt processing for a medium 7B model falling to a poor 10.33 tokens/sec. This hardware profile is best suited for entry-level GPU-accelerated workloads, small-scale model inference, lightweight graphics rendering, or development environments rather than heavy multi-threaded compute or large-scale database operations.
